role: Exploratory assessment requested after the prior feasibility results; not an untouched confirmatory experiment
source: Same existing development sample, one review per author and independent preference after removing the input-book history
schemes: Three book-disjoint folds on all three target groups
Same three folds restricted to reviews of Thriller books, preserving the existing independently measured preference
models: Same unweighted logistic style/words/combined models, diagnostic context models, and count-based naive Bayes as the previous study
primary_algorithm: Naive Bayes, selected before running the three-group experiment based on the previous feasibility study; model comparison is exploratory
preprocessing_and_tuning: Exactly the existing fold-local functions and regularization grid, no additional features or options
metrics: Macro-F1, balanced accuracy, per-group precision/recall/F1, majority and frequency-based baselines
uncertainty: 2000 paired bootstrap resamples of book titles, out-of-fold predictions fixed
analyst_feasibility_criterion: On the full three-group cohort, primary macro-F1 >=0.50, balanced accuracy >=0.50, each class recall >=0.30, and >=0.10 improvement over both baselines in both metrics with paired 95% lower bounds >0
interpretation: Passing the predictive criterion supports a three-group research question in this cohort. Prediction from stable personal writing style independently of book topic requires additional support. The common-input-genre subset is reported separately and will be substantially imbalanced.
scope_change: Do not silently replace the current amendment before reporting this assessment. Preserve original Phase 1 files.
